questions.stem: A unitary system of government is one in which

options.text: all constitutional powers are concentrated in one central government
powers are divided between a central government and component states by the constitution
sovereign states form a loose union and may withdraw at will
the executive is drawn from and answerable to the legislature

questions.explanation: In a unitary state there is only one source of constitutional authority. Local bodies exist because the centre created them, exercise only delegated functions, and can be reorganised or abolished by the centre.

distractorRationale.d: That describes the parliamentary system, which answers a different question about government

questions.stem: Which of the following is an essential requirement of a federal system of government?

options.text: A single-chamber legislature at the centre
A written and rigid constitution dividing powers between the tiers
A hereditary head of state
The right of every component unit to secede

questions.explanation: The division of powers must be written down and hard to alter, otherwise the centre could simply legislate away the states' sphere. A supreme court is then needed to police the boundary between the two levels.

distractorRationale.a: Federations normally use a bicameral legislature so that the units are separately represented
distractorRationale.c: Federations may be republics or monarchies; headship of state is irrelevant to the classification
distractorRationale.d: A right of secession belongs to confederations; federations do not recognise it

questions.stem: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, matters on which both the National Assembly and a State House of Assembly may legislate are contained in the

options.text: Exclusive Legislative List
Concurrent Legislative List
Residual List
Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles

questions.explanation: The Concurrent Legislative List covers shared subjects such as education, health, agriculture and electricity. Where a valid federal law conflicts with a state law on a concurrent matter, the federal law prevails.

distractorRationale.a: The Exclusive List is reserved to the National Assembly alone, covering defence, currency, mines and minerals and similar subjects
distractorRationale.c: Residual matters are not listed at all and belong to the states alone
distractorRationale.d: Chapter II of the Constitution sets out national goals rather than legislative competence

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), Second Schedule

questions.stem: The main difference between a federation and a confederation is that in a confederation

options.text: the component states retain their sovereignty and may withdraw
the central government is stronger than the component states
there must be a written and rigid constitution
the supreme court settles all disputes between the tiers

questions.explanation: A confederation is created by sovereign states that keep their sovereignty and lend limited powers to the centre. That is why withdrawal is normally permitted, whereas a federation's units are not sovereign and cannot lawfully secede.

distractorRationale.b: The centre is deliberately weak in a confederation; a strong centre points towards a federation
distractorRationale.c: A rigid written constitution is a mark of federalism; confederations rest on a treaty
distractorRationale.d: Judicial settlement of intergovernmental disputes is a federal device

questions.stem: Which factor most strongly explains Nigeria's adoption of a federal system?

options.text: Its membership of the Commonwealth
Its large size and wide ethnic and cultural diversity
Its dependence on crude oil exports
Its use of English as an official language

questions.explanation: Federalism is the standard device for holding together a large, plural society: it grants each major group a protected sphere so that unity does not require uniformity. Nigeria's regionalisation from 1946 onwards was driven precisely by size and diversity.

distractorRationale.a: The Commonwealth contains unitary members such as Ghana and federal members such as Canada, so it explains nothing
distractorRationale.c: Oil shaped revenue allocation disputes within the federation but came long after the federal structure was adopted
distractorRationale.d: A shared official language would, if anything, make a unitary system easier

questions.stem: Which of the following is a genuine advantage of a unitary system over a federal one?

options.text: It guarantees each region a protected sphere of authority
It avoids the cost of duplicating governments and reduces jurisdictional disputes
It gives component units the right to make their own constitutions
It requires a supreme court to arbitrate between tiers of government

questions.explanation: With one legislature, one executive and one set of laws, a unitary state avoids maintaining parallel structures and never has to litigate who may legislate on what. Cheapness and uniformity are its strongest claims.

distractorRationale.a: Protected regional spheres are a federal feature; in a unitary state local powers are revocable
distractorRationale.c: Only federal component units may have their own constitutions, as American states do
distractorRationale.d: The need for judicial arbitration is a consequence of federal division, not a unitary advantage

questions.stem: In a federation, the component units are sovereign states in international law.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. Sovereignty in a federation belongs to the federation as a whole; the units exercise only the powers the constitution allocates to them and have no separate international personality. Only in a confederation do the members remain sovereign.

distractorRationale.a: This confuses constitutional autonomy with sovereignty; Lagos State has powers but cannot sign treaties or declare war

questions.stem: Nigeria was formally established as a federation by the

options.text: Clifford Constitution of 1922
Richards Constitution of 1946
Lyttleton Constitution of 1954
Independence Constitution of 1960

questions.explanation: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 was the first to describe Nigeria as a federation, giving the regions genuine legislative and executive autonomy with a defined division of powers. Earlier constitutions had prepared the ground without completing the change.

distractorRationale.a: Clifford's 1922 Constitution introduced the elective principle to a legislative council, not federalism
distractorRationale.b: Richards in 1946 introduced regionalism through regional houses of assembly, but they were advisory and the system remained unitary
distractorRationale.d: The 1960 Constitution continued the federal structure that 1954 had already created
